subject.title: [Bug] web_fetch fails in dual-stack networks when DNS returns IPv6 special-use addresses

question: Should `web_fetch` allow a hostname when DNS returns a mix of blocked special-use addresses and at least one allowed public address, provided blocked addresses are removed from the pinned connection pool?
rationale: The proposed fix relaxes the current default SSRF decision from any-blocked-answer denial to all-blocked-answer denial, which is a security-boundary policy choice that automation should not make without maintainer intent.

options.title: Allow mixed answers after filtering
options.body: Treat mixed DNS answers as allowed only when at least one public address remains and ensure blocked addresses cannot be used downstream.

options.title: Keep strict any-blocked denial
options.body: Preserve the current fail-closed SSRF behavior and document the dual-stack/DNS-pollution limitation or workaround.

options.title: Add opt-in policy surface
options.body: Keep the strict default and add a reviewed explicit configuration path for operators who need mixed-answer tolerance.

recommendation.title: Allow mixed answers after filtering
recommendation.body: Treat mixed DNS answers as allowed only when at least one public address remains and ensure blocked addresses cannot be used downstream.
